tools.name: get_loan_officer
tools.description: Returns one loan officer's bluerate.ai profile by NMLS ID: name, company, licensed states, loan types, languages, about text, up to 3 client reviews, FAQs and url: the loan officer's public bluerate profile, where people request a callback. Contains no phone numbers or email addresses.

tools.name: request_callback
tools.description: Creates a one-time bluerate.ai link (confirmationUrl, valid for 24 hours) for asking a loan officer listed on bluerate.ai to call back. The person who wants the call opens the link, enters their own phone number and email, agrees to be contacted and submits; only then is the loan officer notified. P

tools.name: search_loan_officers
tools.description: Searches licensed US mortgage loan officers listed on bluerate.ai by state, optionally near a city or ZIP code, for a loan type (conventional, FHA, VA, USDA, jumbo, non-QM, home equity: HELOC or home equity loan) or by a language they speak. Returns up to 10 loan officers, each with name, NMLS ID, c

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_loan_officer, search_loan_officers · Public sink: get_loan_officer, request_callback, search_loan_officers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_loan_officer, search_loan_officers · Public sink: get_loan_officer, request_callback, search_loan_officers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_loan_officers" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
